text:
maria: heads up — after merging Orchid's LoRA into deployable v3.2 and running q4_0 quant on the host, the quick-eval pack shows a small but consistent quality drop on the customer intent suite.
sam: how small? numbers?
maria: on intent_accuracy: baseline (fp16+adapter) 92.1% -> post-merge q4_0 89.7%.
lex: that's larger than typical quant noise. Is the evalpack the same seeds and prompt templates?
maria: yes — evalpack-v2, same prompts, same detokenization. ran 3 seeds.
matt: any diffs on short vs long context?
maria: interesting — short ctx (<=512) drop is ~1.8 points; long ctx (2k-4k) drop ~3.1 points. also saw higher repetition on multi-turn.
jiang: customer noticed hallucination uptick in long conversations yesterday. they reported it as intermittent.
sam: could be KV cache or attention kernel mismatch with adapter merge + q4 profile. did you try q4_1 or q8_0?
maria: tried q4_1 quickly: accuracy 90.6% (better but still ~1.5 down). q8_0 matches fp16 within noise.
lex: run a small bisect: fp16+adapter (good), fp16+adapter-merged (good), then merged+q4_0 (bad). So merge + q4 seems to interact.
matt: do we have model hashes and merge order recorded? we should reproduce exact merge steps.
maria: merge script: adapter-stitch --base orchid/base-1.9 --lora orchid/lora-idx-7 --alpha 0.5 --order lora-first. commit: c7f3a9. I pushed the merged weights to s3://redwood-prod/orchid/merged/v3.2.
sam: try re-merging with order base-first and alpha=0.7 — sometimes numerical mixing order changes out-of-range activations that quant rounds differently.
lex: also try soft-clamp before quant: run clamp-activations --p=0.999 on logits layer then quant. we've seen that reduce long-context drift.
maria: running re-merge + clamping now. ETA ~30m. putting quick eval command here:
```bash
python eval/run_quick_eval.py \
  --model s3://redwood-prod/orchid/merged/v3.2-retest \
  --quant-profile q4_0 \
  --evalpack evalpack-v2/intent_long_ctx.jsonl \
  --seeds 3 \
  --out results/orchid_q4_retest.json
```
dev-bot: CI: load-test for model/merge c7f3a9 started — https://ci.redwood.dev/12345 (status: running)
sam: also add a tiny synthetic suite that isolates KV cache hits (prefix-replay tests). helps confirm if caching is amplifying error.
maria: good call — spinning that up too.
(40m later)
maria: results: re-merge order base-first + alpha=0.7 + clamp p=0.999 -> q4_0 accuracy 91.3% on long ctx, short ctx 91.9%. still ~0.8 down vs fp16 but within acceptable threshold for this customer.
jiang: customer ops — is that acceptable? they asked for <1% regression.
matt: 0.8% is borderline; propose we ship a canary to Dedicated pool with fallback to fp16 for any session that exceeds 2k tokens.
sam: implement routing policy: if ctx_len>2048 -> route to fp16 variant; else use q4_0 merged. add a safety metric to console to auto-fallback if hallucination rate crosses threshold.
lex: we should also create a quant-profile ticket to refine q4 settings for Orchid — sounds like a customer-specific quant profile is warranted.
maria: opening ticket: QP-1847 (orchid custom q4 profile + merge heuristics). also saving eval artifacts to s3://redwood-results/orchid/1865004321.
matt: thanks — I'll message the customer with the proposed canary + fallback plan.
jiang: I'll coordinate the rollout window and note the change log.
sam: follow-up tests: reproduce on dedicated GPUs (A10G) and on customer on-prem staging if available — quant rounding differs by kernel sometimes.
maria: noted. will run dedicated infra tests next.
lex: short-term hypothesis: numeric interaction between merge alpha + weight ordering produces outlier activations at deeper layers; q4 quantization then amplifies error in long-range attention. mitigation: clamp + order change + routing rules.
maria: summary: found regression after merge+q4; re-merge + clamp improved; we will canary with routing fallback. created ticket QP-1847. artifacts + logs in s3. will follow up once dedicated tests pass.
matt: :thumbsup:
jiang: thanks all.
